_comment: Private corpus for the demo user 'test1'. NOT part of the shared library.
The persona: a working game developer who has been to a few conferences and
keeps a reading list. These are the talks they sat in and the articles they
saved — their own material, ingested into their own corpus, searchable only
Ingest with:  python scripts/ingest.py --manifest corpus/test1_sources.json --owner test1
Chosen so the ECS question has more than one credible answer in it. A corpus
where every source agrees cannot demonstrate anything about handling
disagreement — so the critique of the entity-component model is in here
deliberately, sitting next to the talks that advocate for it.
Everything here is freely published on the open web. Corpus policy still
applies to the shared library; see README.md.

Not here on purpose: gamedev.net's 'A Critique of the Entity Component Model' returns 403 to automated fetches. That is the site declining to be crawled, so it stays out. Two other counter-positions cover the same ground.

Second batch (24 Aug 2026) targets 'how do I optimize performance from externally imported 3D model assets'. Chosen for genuine disagreement: Unity's manual says author an LOD chain, Unreal's Nanite docs say use no LODs at all, and meshoptimizer's author says mesh compression does not improve runtime performance at scale. gamedeveloper.com's 'GPU Performance for Game Artists' was wanted and rejected: its robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot, GPTBot and CCBot with 'Disallow: /'.

sources.title: A Data Oriented Approach to Using Component Systems (Unity at GDC 2018)
sources.author: Mike Acton
sources.note: Attended GDC 2018. The strongest case for the data-oriented reading of ECS.

sources.title: Understanding Data-Oriented Design for Entity Component Systems (Unity at GDC 2019)
sources.author: Unity Technologies
sources.note: Attended GDC 2019. Explains why the memory layout is the point, not the API.

sources.title: Building a Data-Oriented Future
sources.author: Mike Acton
sources.note: Saved. The general argument, outside any one engine.

sources.title: Entity Component System FAQ
sources.author: Sander Mertens
sources.note: The reference text on ECS implementation strategies: archetype vs sparse set vs bitset.

sources.title: Flecs FAQ
sources.author: Sander Mertens
sources.note: Archetype ECS in practice, from the author of one.

sources.title: Data Oriented Design — An Interpretation
sources.author: Sebastian Schöner
sources.note: Saved. Sympathetic but sceptical: separates the cache argument from the ECS argument.

sources.title: bevy_ecs — README
sources.author: Bevy contributors
sources.note: A production archetype ECS, documented by its authors.

sources.title: ecs-faq — source repository
sources.author: Sander Mertens
sources.note: Saved for the reading list at the bottom.

sources.title: Archetypal ECS Considered Harmful?
sources.note: Saved as a counter-position. Argues the benchmark wins belong to archetypal ECS specifically, and are far from universal.

sources.title: Why I Removed Components From My Game
sources.author: Joshua Manton
sources.note: Saved as a counter-position. Calls the composition and performance arguments half-truths for games with a known set of object types.

sources.title: meshoptimizer — mesh optimization library
sources.author: Arseny Kapoulkine
sources.note: Saved. Vertex cache/fetch/overdraw optimisation and simplification, from the author of the library most pipelines use.

sources.title: meshoptimizer — source repository
sources.author: Arseny Kapoulkine
sources.note: Saved. Deliberately kept alongside the site above to exercise near-duplicate detection.

sources.title: Billions of Triangles in Minutes
sources.author: Arseny Kapoulkine
sources.note: Saved. Cluster LOD generation at scale — what actually costs time when preprocessing imported geometry.

sources.title: Float Compression 4: Mesh Optimizer
sources.author: Aras Pranckevičius
sources.note: Saved. Measures mesh compression rather than asserting it — separates file size from runtime cost.

sources.title: Unity Manual — Optimizing draw calls
sources.note: Saved. Batching, instancing, and why reducing triangles does not reduce draw calls.

sources.title: Unity Manual — Level of Detail (LOD)
sources.note: Saved. The author-your-own-LOD-chain position.

sources.title: Nanite Virtualized Geometry in Unreal Engine
sources.note: Saved as the counter-position: Nanite static meshes use no LODs at all.

sources.title: Nanite Technical Details
sources.note: Saved. Cluster hierarchy, vertex quantisation, and the fallback mesh — where the import settings actually land.

sources.title: Mesh shaders on AMD RDNA graphics cards
sources.author: AMD GPUOpen
sources.note: Saved. The hardware side — why cluster-shaped geometry is the thing modern GPUs want.

sources.title: glTF Transform
sources.author: Don McCurdy
sources.note: Saved. The practical toolchain for reprocessing an imported glTF: dedup, weld, quantize, compress.

sources.title: Draco 3D data compression
sources.author: Google
sources.note: Saved. The other compression option, so the trade-off against meshopt has both sides present.

sources.title: Art Optimization: How Fatshark Built Their Central Asset Pipeline
sources.note: Attended. A shipped studio's asset pipeline for Darktide — the production view, not the library view.
